FROMLIST: ASoC: amd: pte offset related dma driver changes Added pte offset variable in audio_substream_data structure. Added Stoney related PTE offset macros in acp header file. Modified hw_params callback to assign the pte offset value based on asic_type. PTE Offset macros used to calculate no of PTE entries need to be programmed when memory allocated for audio buffer. FROMGIT: mmc: sdhci-msm: support voltage pad switching The PADs for SD card are dual-voltage that support 3v/1.8v. Those PADs have a control signal (io_pad_pwr_switch/mode18 ) that indicates whether the PAD works in 3v or 1.8v. SDHC core on msm platforms should have IO_PAD_PWR_SWITCH bit set/unset based on actual voltage used for IO lines. So when power irq is triggered for io high or io low, the driver should check the voltages supported and set the pad accordingly. Signed-off-by: Krishna Konda <kkonda@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Venkat Gopalakrishnan <venkatg@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Vijay Viswanath <vviswana@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Acked-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org> BUG=b:74258835 TEST=Build kernel for Cheza Change-Id: I77b75aa9d6ce518b2c4301140c091529e28a0971 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 9e9356de51beea7763ee8852c4e11c155fa3ab1a git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/ulfh/mmc.git next) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/917875 Commit-Ready: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org>

llvm: force llvm to die if implicit blacklist files not found. The cherry-picks an upstream patch to force LLVM to die if the implicit blacklist files cannot be found. The commit message is commit 23ea169fe0e4316bf621c6a690900c8a7d9f8707 Author: Peter Collingbourne <peter@pcc.me.uk> Date: Mon May 7 20:54:05 2018 +0000 [CFI] Force LLVM to die if the implicit blacklist files cannot be found. Currently LLVM CFI tries to use an implicit blacklist file, currently in /usr/lib64/clang/<version>/share. If the file is not there, LLVM happily continues, which causes CFI to add checks to files/functions that are known to fail, generating binaries that fail. This CL causes LLVM to die (I hope) if it can't find these implicit blacklist files. Patch by Caroline Tice! BUG=None TEST=sudo emerge llvm Change-Id: I7c9793b5d1aa2a4750e5bf2274fd4cf7933343ef Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1050407 Commit-Ready: Yunlian Jiang <yunlian@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yunlian Jiang <yunlian@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Manoj Gupta <manojgupta@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Caroline Tice <cmtice@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Improve LE Credential free label finding scheme This patch modifies the GetFreeLabel() to generate a random new label instead of just a monotonically increasing value. This ensures that the labels are spread more evenly across the entire hash tree. This helps in a out-of-sync situation where the first label being out of sync would always make the entire tree out-of-sync. This patch also adds a unit test to test the change required in PersistentLookupTable. BUG=chromium:809718, chromium:809703 TEST=1. cros_run_unit tests 2. Make several new keys using CLI, and verify that the key labels in the low_entropy_creds directory are random. Change-Id: I017a75b657b710c74a1868aa14eca58fcd9e3363 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1045503 Commit-Ready: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Tested-by: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Reviewed-by: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com>

But in npcx7 series, there are two chip generations and it's better to show chip generation information by 'version' console command. In this CL, we used SRID_CR to distinguish the generation of npcx7 series. It also adds the support for NPCX787G in system_get_chip_name() since it is used on the version 1 of npcx7 evb. sign_official_build: switch kernel/firmware signing to loopdevs Newer versions of util-linux/mount don't like when you create overlapping loopback files. Since we always create a loopback of the entire image, this means every mount fails. We can change the few users in here over to using the existing loopback partitions rather than continuing to create their own from scratch. This makes the code a bit simpler. However, we currently duplicate some of the mount image helpers so that one version works off of a disk image while the other uses loopbacks. Cleaning this up requires a number of changes in other files which we'll want to do eventually, just not right now (to minimize risk).
